question.value: Do spiral arms enhance star formation efficiency, or only gather gas? Measured via arm/interarm contrasts in stellar mass, molecular gas, SFR and SFE at ~100 pc in 28 PHANGS spiral galaxies

evidence.quote: Here, we aim to examine this problem in greater detail by assembling a comprehensive set of homogeneous measurements of spiral arm-to-interarm contrasts in stellar mass, gas, SFR, and SFE

referee_caveats_inferred: The SFE conclusion depends on an empirical Halpha extinction calibration derived on 13 galaxies and applied to all, plus a fixed alpha_CO and R21.
Arm/interarm definition rests on pre-existing masks whose interarm ring includes inner rings and bar ends, which biases SFR contrasts low at small radii.
Radial bins within a galaxy are not independent, so the 4 sigma significance on the median SFE contrast probably overstates the evidence.

reproducibility.score_reason: Public CO products and published masks allow a partial redo, but Halpha maps, SFR calibration details and several choices are inherited or in prep., and no code is released.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The ALMA CO products and masks are public and results are numeric, but the Halpha SFR maps are unpublished and recipe details are missing, so a full redo is not possible from the paper alone.
